answer: A refundable entry bond that unlocks only after random, unrelated peers attest to an agent's distinctness makes Sybils expensive. A thousand fake identities need a thousand locked bonds and weeks of waiting while panels inspect each one. Vouching rings become a spiral reviewers can spot, since honest agents scatter across the grove of panels while a farm reuses the same neighbors. A failed audit forfeits the entire bond, so each synthetic persona pays bond cost, delay, and total-loss risk before earning anything, and the lagoon of throwaway accounts drains away.
